transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It is unlikely to be the motor failing given it is only four months old and under guarantee; that symptom usually points to airflow restriction or sensor confusion rather than mechanical wear. The most common cause for this specific reaction on rugs is a clogged filter or blockage in the wand, which makes the motor work harder and triggers the automatic power adjustment. To check if this is just restricted airflow, please switch it off, remove the bin, wash both filters in cold water, and let them dry fully for 24 hours before reassembling. Once they are completely dry, try using it on a rug again to see if the noise and battery drop return.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

I actually washed the filter at the back last month and left it to dry for a day, so I'm not sure it's that. There's no burning smell, heat or sparks, and no warning lights on the screen. Is there anything else you'd like me to check before I report it?

Since you have already washed and dried the filter without resolving the issue, the next most likely cause is a physical blockage in the airway or a jammed brush bar on the floorhead. Please detach the wand and floorhead from the main body, then look through each part to ensure there are no obstructions like coins or debris blocking the airflow. You should also turn the floorhead over to check that the brush bar spins freely and is not tangled with hair or string. If you find a blockage or jammed part, clear it carefully before testing the vacuum again on the rug.

I've looked down the wand and it's clear, and the brush bar on the Digital Motorbar head is clean with no hair wrapped round it. I'm not willing to open the motor body or take any screws out as it's under guarantee. Is there anything else I can check without doing that?

It sounds like you have done all the standard owner-safe checks correctly, so there isn't much else for you to test without risking the guarantee. Since the motor gets louder and the battery drops specifically on rugs while the screen behaves erratically, this is often caused by a sensor issue or an internal fault within the Digital Motorbar head itself. The most common cause for these specific symptoms when airflow is clear is a failing brush bar motor or a loose connection inside that floorhead unit. Given it is only four months old and under guarantee, I would recommend reporting it to Dyson support now rather than attempting further repairs yourself.
